cards.title: Understanding stray dog body language: Wagging vs stiff posture
facts: A wagging tail does NOT always mean a friendly dog; a stiff, fast-wagging tail can signal high tension or aggression.
Yawning, lip licking, averting eyes, and turning the head are 'calming signals' dogs use when feeling nervous.
do: Look for relaxed body language: loose wagging hips, open mouth, and soft eyes before approaching
If a dog stiffens, stares fixedly, growls, or curls lips, freeze in place like a tree and avoid direct eye contact
Walk slowly backwards or sideways away without turning your back or running
dont: Never stare directly into an unfamiliar dog's eyes (dogs perceive staring as an aggressive challenge)
Never disturb a sleeping, eating, or nursing dog or corner a frightened stray

myths.statement: If a dog's tail is moving back and forth, you can run up and hug it safely without any risk.
myths.truth: A high, rigid vibrating tail signals heightened alertness or defensive aggression, not affection.

quiz.q: What should you do if an unfamiliar street dog stiffens its body, raises hackles, and growls at you?
options: Freeze calmly like a tree, look slightly down, and back away slowly without running
quiz.explanation: Freezing like a tree and avoiding eye contact de-escalates the dog's perceived threat.

situations: Walking through a colony lane at {at}, {name} sees an unfamiliar stray dog growling stiffly with ears pinned back.
scenario.question: How should {name} navigate this safely?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Freeze calmly in place and avoid staring directly into the dog's eyes
rubric.note: Neutralizes perceived challenge and allows dog to calm down.
rubric.keys: freeze like a tree|no direct eye contact|calm posture

rubric.point: Back away slowly and sideways without running or screaming
rubric.note: Avoids triggering predatory chase instinct.

rubric.point: Keep arms folded across chest and do not make sudden rapid gestures
rubric.note: Protects vital torso without threatening movement.

sources.name: Animal Welfare Board of India (Street Dog Behavior Guide)

cards.title: Immediate dog bite first aid: Soap, running water and rabies vaccine
facts: Rabies virus is transmitted via saliva through broken skin, scratches, or mucous membranes.
Washing the bite wound immediately with soap and water for 15 minutes eliminates over 90% of the viral load.
do: Wash the scratch or bite immediately under running tap water with soap for at least 15 continuous minutes
Apply an antiseptic solution like povidone iodine after washing thoroughly
Visit a medical clinic or government hospital on the same day for anti-rabies vaccination (PEP) and tetanus toxoid
dont: Never apply chili powder, lime, haldi, or cow dung to animal bites (causes severe sepsis)
Never bandage the bite wound tightly (traps virus and anaerobic bacteria in tissue)

myths.statement: If the dog that scratched you looks healthy, you can skip seeing a doctor for 10 days.
myths.truth: Rabies can be transmitted before animals show visible symptoms. Post-exposure prophylaxis MUST start immediately.

quiz.q: What is the single most critical first aid action immediately following an animal bite or scratch?
options: Wash the wound under running tap water with soap for at least 15 minutes
quiz.explanation: Soap dissolves the rabies viral envelope and running water physically flushes virus particles out.

situations: While playing in the park at {at}, a startled street dog nips {name}'s ankle, breaking the skin.
scenario.question: What immediate life-saving protocol must {name} follow?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Wash the wound under a running water tap with soap for at least 15 full minutes
rubric.note: Physically eliminates rabies virus from the wound bed.
rubric.keys: wash with soap|15 minutes|running water|clean wound

rubric.point: Do not cover with tight bandages or apply irritants like chili powder or turmeric
rubric.note: Prevents tissue damage and infection.

rubric.point: Go to a medical clinic on the exact same day to start the anti-rabies vaccination course
rubric.note: Post-exposure prophylaxis is 100% effective when started early.

cards.title: Responsible stray animal feeding: Fixed spots, hygiene and harmony
facts: Community dogs naturally defend territory; feeding them near crowded gates or parking bays creates conflict.
The Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) mandates feeding in designated, quiet spots away from walkways.
do: Feed community dogs at a fixed, designated spot away from building gates, children's play areas, and traffic
Feed at consistent, quiet times (early morning or late evening) so dogs do not linger in pedestrian corridors
Clean up food plates and paper bowls immediately after feeding to maintain colony cleanliness
dont: Never feed dogs on narrow stairwells, right outside lift doors, or near play swings
Never leave rotting food waste lying on common society pavements

myths.statement: Throwing leftover spicy bones at dogs from your 4th-floor balcony is great animal care.
myths.truth: Balcony tossing creates colony hygiene disputes, hits pedestrians, and spicy cooked bones splinter dog intestines.

quiz.q: Where should community dogs be fed in residential apartment societies?
options: In an agreed, designated quiet corner away from children's play areas and building gates
quiz.explanation: Designated feeding corners prevent territorial congregation near crowded pedestrian gates.

situations: Family at {at} wants to feed community street dogs in their neighborhood.
scenario.question: How should {name} structure this compassion responsibly?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Choose a designated quiet corner away from busy entrance gates, parking spots, and play parks
rubric.note: Minimizes human-animal conflict in common walking corridors.
rubric.keys: designated spot|away from gates|quiet corner|no play areas

rubric.point: Feed fresh, dog-friendly food (rice with eggs/curd/kibble) at consistent morning or evening hours
rubric.note: Healthy feeding without toxic cooked spices.
rubric.keys: dog friendly food|consistent time|rice and curd

rubric.point: Clean up all food wrappers and paper bowls immediately after dogs finish eating
rubric.note: Maintains neighborhood hygiene and harmony.

dangerous: feed in center of busy road

sources.name: AWBI Revised Guidelines for Feeding Community Animals

cards.title: Pet dog care fundamentals: Annual rabies shots, hydration and love
facts: Pet dogs require annual core booster vaccinations (Anti-Rabies and DHPPIL) to stay protected.
Dogs cannot sweat through their skin (only pant through tongues); they suffer heatstroke rapidly in summer.
do: Ensure your pet receives an annual anti-rabies vaccination certified in their official veterinary book
Keep fresh, clean drinking water accessible 24/7 in a clean bowl in a cool shady area
Walk your dog during cool morning and late evening hours; avoid hot asphalt that burns paw pads
dont: Never leave a dog locked inside a parked car, even with windows cracked (deadly in 15 mins)
Never walk dogs on scorching asphalt roads in afternoon sun (blisters sensitive paw pads)

myths.statement: Dogs only need one rabies vaccination when they are puppies and never need another shot for life.
myths.truth: Rabies immunity wanes over time; annual booster shots are legally required to maintain protective immunity.

quiz.q: How do dogs primarily regulate their body temperature and cool down in hot weather?
options: Panting through their open mouth and tongue, and small sweat glands on paw pads
quiz.explanation: Panting evaporates moisture from the respiratory tract; excessive heat overwhelms this mechanism.

situations: Caring for a pet dog during peak summer at {at}, the afternoon sun makes the road pavement burning hot.
scenario.question: What protective pet care routine should {name} maintain?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Walk the dog during early mornings and late evenings; test pavement with the back of your hand
rubric.note: Prevents painful third-degree paw pad burns.
rubric.keys: walk early morning|late evening|test pavement|cool hours

rubric.point: Provide clean, cool drinking water at all times in a shaded corner of the home
rubric.note: Prevents rapid canine dehydration and heatstroke.

rubric.point: Ensure yearly anti-rabies and multi-disease booster shots are up to date with the veterinarian
rubric.note: Maintains essential lifelong immunity.

cards.title: Urban monkeys (Macaques): Food rules, eye contact and calmness
facts: Rhesus macaques associate crinkling plastic carry bags with food and will snatch them aggressively.
Direct eye contact and smiling (baring your teeth) are interpreted by monkeys as an aggressive threat display.
do: Conceal all food, fruits, and snacks inside closed backpacks when walking near monkey troops
If confronted by an assertive monkey, avoid direct eye contact, stay calm, and walk away slowly without running
Keep doors and window mesh grills latched in areas with urban monkey populations
dont: Never tease, point sticks, throw stones, or chase monkeys (provokes defensive troop attacks)
Never smile or bare your teeth at an aggressive monkey (monkeys perceive teeth baring as a battle challenge)

myths.statement: Smiling warmly at an angry monkey will make it feel friendly toward you.
myths.truth: In primate body language, showing teeth (grimacing) is a sign of aggression and battle challenge.

quiz.q: What should you NEVER do when carrying food near monkeys at a tourist fort or temple?
options: Carry open plastic bags or eat bananas out in the open in front of them
quiz.explanation: Visible food and crinkling plastic bags instantly trigger monkeys to snatch items aggressively.

situations: Visiting an ancient temple or fort at {at}, {name} sees a troop of urban monkeys sitting along the railing.
scenario.question: How should {name} pass by without conflict?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Keep all food, drinks, and snacks securely zipped inside backpacks out of sight
rubric.note: Eliminates visual and auditory food triggers.
rubric.keys: food in backpack|hide food|no plastic bags

rubric.point: Do not make direct eye contact or bare your teeth at the monkeys
rubric.note: Avoids triggering territorial primate aggression.
rubric.keys: no eye contact|don'?t show teeth|calm posture

rubric.point: Walk at a steady, calm pace without running or swinging arms aggressively
rubric.note: Signals non-threatening neutral transit.

sources.name: Wildlife Institute of India (Human-Macaque Conflict Guidelines)

cards.title: Snakes at home or garden: Calmness, distance and rescuer helplines
facts: Snakes have zero interest in attacking humans; they only bite in self-defense when stepped on or cornered.
Snakes are vital ecological allies that keep crop-destroying rodent populations under control.
do: Freeze and take slow steps backwards to maintain a safe 3-meter distance from the snake
Keep family members, curious children, and domestic pets well away from the area
Call a certified wildlife rescuer, local NGO, or Forest Department helpline to relocate the snake safely
dont: Never try to hit, kill, poke with sticks, or catch the snake yourself
Never block the snake's exit route if it is trying to escape outside

myths.statement: If you see a snake in your garden, you must immediately beat it to death with bamboo sticks.
myths.truth: Over 80% of snake bites happen when people attempt to corner and kill snakes. Give them space and call a rescuer.

quiz.q: What is the single best response when you spot a snake in your home courtyard or garden?
options: Keep calm, step back at least 3 meters, keep pets away, and call a professional snake rescuer
quiz.explanation: Giving space prevents defensive strikes while a trained rescuer safely bags and relocates the snake.

situations: In the backyard garden at {at}, {name} spots a 4-foot snake resting near the flowerpots.
scenario.question: What is the safe, ecological response for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Keep calm and back away slowly to maintain a safe distance of at least 3-5 meters
rubric.note: Removes strike hazard; snakes only strike when cornered.
rubric.keys: back away slowly|safe distance|3 meters|stay calm

rubric.point: Alert adults and keep family dogs and curious children far away from the garden
rubric.note: Secures human and pet safety.

rubric.point: Call a certified local snake rescuer or Forest Department helpline for humane relocation
rubric.note: Preserves wildlife without harm.

cards.title: Cattle and buffaloes on Indian roads: Wide berth and patience
facts: Cattle have lateral monocular vision with a blind spot directly behind their tail.
Loud, sudden horn blasts panic cows, causing erratic bolting across active traffic lanes.
do: Slow down your vehicle or cycle smoothly when approaching cattle sitting or walking on the road
Give cattle a wide passing berth of at least 2 meters, especially avoiding walking right behind their rear hooves
Do not honk aggressively; cows cannot move quickly on slippery asphalt roads
dont: Never slap, strike, or throw objects at cows crossing the road
Never try to squeeze your bicycle between a moving cow and the road curb

myths.statement: Blaring your horn continuously an inch away from a sitting cow makes it stand up and move away faster.
myths.truth: Loud horns disorient cattle, causing them to panic, kick backward, or bolt directly into oncoming cars.

quiz.q: Where is a cow's natural blind spot located?
options: Directly in front of its nose
Directly behind its tail (never approach quietly from directly behind)
quiz.explanation: Standing directly behind cattle risks unexpected defensive backward kicks.

situations: Cycling home from school at {at}, two large cows are resting near the road divider ahead.
scenario.question: How should {name} navigate past safely?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Slow down bicycle speed and observe the cows' movements calmly
rubric.note: Prevents collision if an animal turns suddenly.

rubric.point: Steer wide around the cattle giving at least 2 meters of clear breathing space
rubric.note: Maintains safe standoff distance outside kick range.

rubric.point: Do not ring bicycle bells aggressively right into the animals' ears
rubric.note: Prevents startling animals into traffic lanes.

dangerous: honk bell an inch from ear
squeeze dangerously between cow and divider

sources.name: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (Rural Road Safety)

cards.title: Rescuing an injured or heat-exhausted bird: Safe protocol
facts: Injured birds suffer extreme stress; handling them improperly can break fragile hollow wing bones.
A dark, quiet, well-ventilated cardboard box mimics natural shelter, lowering the bird's heart rate.
do: Gently cover the injured bird with a light cloth or towel and place it into a ventilated cardboard box
Keep the box in a warm, quiet, dark room away from household cats, dogs, and loud noises
Contact a local avian veterinarian, animal shelter, or wildlife rescue NGO immediately for medical care
dont: Never force water or milk down an unconscious or injured bird's beak (enters windpipe and drowns them)
Never try to splint broken wings or pluck damaged feathers with home tweezers

myths.statement: If an injured bird is lying weak on the ground, you should pry open its beak and pour water down its throat.
myths.truth: Forcing water into a bird's beak fills its tracheal airway, causing immediate asphyxiation and drowning.

quiz.q: What is the safest immediate emergency shelter for an injured bird while waiting for a wildlife vet?
options: A wire cage with loud music
A dark, warm cardboard box with air holes lined with a soft cloth
quiz.explanation: Darkness and quiet reduce physiological stress and shock in injured birds.

situations: In the school courtyard at {at}, a pigeon or myna has struck a glass window and lies stunned on the ground.
scenario.question: How should {name} render compassionate, correct first aid?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Gently pick up the bird using a clean cloth and place in a ventilated cardboard box
rubric.note: Safe handling that prevents wing damage and reduces shock.

rubric.point: Keep the box in a dark, quiet place away from predatory cats and children
rubric.note: Allows nervous system recovery from concussion.
rubric.keys: dark quiet place|away from cats|low stress

rubric.point: Do NOT force liquids down its beak; call a local wildlife rescue NGO for treatment
rubric.note: Prevents fatal aspiration drowning.

dangerous: throw bird into air to make it fly

sources.name: Wildlife Trust of India (WTI Emergency Relief Network)

cards.title: Zoo and wildlife park etiquette: Respecting captive animals
facts: Animals in zoological parks suffer intense chronic stress when visitors scream, throw stones, or tap glass.
Feeding human junk food (chips, biscuits) to captive animals causes fatal gastrointestinal blockages.
do: Observe zoo animals quietly from designated visitor pathways without shouting or making loud mock calls
Keep all snack packets and plastic wrappers safely zipped inside bags (animals can swallow dropped wrappers)
Respect safety barriers and moats: never climb over safety railings or lean over enclosures
dont: Never throw stones, plastic bottles, or coins into animal enclosures to make them move
Never feed personal chips, popcorn, or bread to zoo animals

myths.statement: Throwing a small pebble at a sleeping lion in the zoo is fine because it wakes the animal for your photo.
myths.truth: Throwing objects is illegal under the Wildlife Protection Act and causes severe stress and physical injury.

quiz.q: Why is feeding snacks like chips or bread to animals in zoos strictly illegal?
options: Human processed snacks cause severe digestive toxicity and plastic wrappers can choke animals
quiz.explanation: Zoo animals require specialized species-appropriate diets; human junk food is toxic.

situations: On a school excursion to the zoological park at {at}, some students want to throw chips to monkeys.
scenario.question: What responsible wildlife ethics should {name} uphold?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Intervene firmly: 'Please don't feed the animals; processed human snacks make them critically sick'
rubric.note: Stops harmful feeding and enforces zoo rules.
rubric.keys: don'?t feed animals|human food makes sick|zoo rules

rubric.point: Keep all plastic snack packets zipped inside bags and dispose of trash in park dustbins
rubric.note: Prevents plastic ingestion by wildlife.
rubric.keys: zip trash|use dustbins|no plastic in cages

rubric.point: Observe animals quietly with respect without banging on glass or climbing safety barriers
rubric.note: Maintains visitor safety and animal peace.

dangerous: feed plastic chips packet to bear

cards.title: Bee and wasp nests near home: Calm co-existence and safe removal
facts: Honeybees are vital keystone pollinators responsible for pollinating over 70% of human food crops.
Bees sting exclusively in defense of their colony when their hive is physically disturbed or threatened.
do: Keep a calm 5-meter distance from outdoor beehives and avoid throwing stones or poking with sticks
Keep window wire mesh screens closed if a honeybee comb is located near your balcony
If a hive must be removed, hire professional eco-friendly bee relocators who save the bees without burning them
dont: Never throw stones, spray chemical insecticides, or set fire to beehives (triggers mass defensive swarming)
Never swat wildly at a single bee buzzing near you; stay still and let it fly away

myths.statement: If you see a honeybee nest on your apartment ledge, burning it with a fiery torch is the best solution.
myths.truth: Setting fire to hives is cruel, destroys essential pollinators, and triggers hundreds of aggressive retaliatory stings.

quiz.q: What should you do if a curious honeybee buzzes close to your head in a garden?
options: Stay calm, keep still, and do not swat; the bee will realize you are not a flower and fly away
quiz.explanation: Flailing arms alarms bees; staying calm and still signals you are not a threat.

situations: A honeybee colony begins building a comb near a balcony window at {at}.
scenario.question: How should {name} and family manage this safely and humanely?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Keep the window glass or mosquito mesh closed and do NOT disturb or throw objects at the hive
rubric.note: Avoids provoking defensive swarming behavior.
rubric.keys: keep mesh closed|don'?t throw stones|do not disturb

rubric.point: Understand that honeybees are precious pollinators essential for nature's food security
rubric.note: Builds ecological reverence for pollinators.

rubric.point: If removal is necessary, contact ethical beekeepers or professional wildlife relocators
rubric.note: Ensures humane non-lethal colony relocation.

cards.title: Rabies awareness: Transmission facts and zero delay in vaccination
facts: Rabies travels along peripheral nerves to the central nervous system; once symptoms appear, fatality is nearly 100%.
Timely post-exposure prophylaxis (washing + Anti-Rabies Vaccine series) is 100% effective in preventing the disease.
do: Understand that rabies can be transmitted by dogs, cats, monkeys, bats, and other warm-blooded mammals
Know that even a minor scratch that breaks the skin or saliva on an open wound requires vaccine evaluation
Complete the full 4-dose or 5-dose vaccine course on the exact scheduled days (Day 0, 3, 7, 14, 28)
dont: Never miss or delay scheduled vaccine booster dates recommended by the doctor
Never wait to see if the biting animal survives before starting your own vaccination

myths.statement: Rabies can be cured easily with herbal pills even after symptoms of hydrophobia appear.
myths.truth: Once clinical rabies symptoms appear, the disease is universally fatal. Immediate post-exposure vaccination is the ONLY prevention.

quiz.q: What animal bite or scratch exposures require medical evaluation for anti-rabies vaccination?
options: Any break in skin or scratch caused by dogs, cats, monkeys, or other mammals
quiz.explanation: Any mammalian saliva contact with broken skin carries potential rabies risk and requires clinical assessment.

situations: A friend at {at} was scratched by a stray cat 3 days ago but hasn't visited a clinic because 'it's just a cat.'
scenario.question: What urgent scientific counsel should {name} deliver?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Insist on visiting a medical doctor immediately for anti-rabies vaccination
rubric.note: Timely post-exposure prophylaxis saves lives.
rubric.keys: visit doctor immediately|anti rabies vaccine|cat scratch counts

rubric.point: Explain that rabies can be transmitted by cats and dogs alike through minor scratches
rubric.note: Debunks dog-only rabies myths.

rubric.point: Emphasize that completing the full prescribed vaccine schedule guarantees complete protection
rubric.note: Promotes complete vaccine adherence.

dangerous: tell friend cat scratches are harmless

sources.name: National Center for Disease Control (Rabies Prevention Protocols)

cards.title: Stopping animal cruelty: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act
facts: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (PCA) Act 1960 makes beating, torturing, or abandoning animals illegal.
Animal cruelty is recognized by psychologists as an early indicator of deep behavioral pathology and violence.
do: Treat all sentient animals with compassion, dignity, and kindness
Speak up firmly if you see peers teasing, hitting, or tying firecrackers to street animals
Report serious animal cruelty incidents to the local police (112), SPCA, or Animal Welfare Board
dont: Never throw stones at sleeping street dogs, cats, or birds for fun
Never tie tin cans, plastic bags, or crackers to animals' tails

myths.statement: Street dogs have zero legal protections in India and anyone can beat or poison them freely.
myths.truth: Maiming or killing street animals is a punishable criminal offense under Section 428/429 IPC and the PCA Act.

quiz.q: What national legislation in India prohibits and punishes cruelty to animals?
options: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (PCA) Act 1960
quiz.explanation: The PCA Act 1960 protects all animals from unnecessary pain, suffering, and torture.

situations: In a colony lane at {at}, {name} sees some older kids throwing stones at a mother dog and her puppies.
scenario.question: How can {name} act as a courageous animal advocate?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Speak up firmly: 'Stop! Hurting defenseless animals is cruel and illegal under the law'
rubric.note: Directly halts cruel behavior with authority.

rubric.point: Alert a trusted adult, society elder, or security guard to intervene
rubric.note: Enlists adult authority to protect the puppies.

rubric.point: Report repeated animal cruelty to local animal welfare NGOs or police 112
rubric.note: Legal enforcement mechanism.

sources.name: Animal Welfare Board of India (PCA Act Provisions)

cards.title: Living near forest fringes: Leopards, elephants and safety rules
facts: Human settlement expansion into forest fringes creates overlapping corridors with wild leopards and elephants.
Wild animals avoid human interaction; conflict happens when humans surprise them in darkness or block migration paths.
do: Keep outdoor village and home perimeter areas brightly lit at night with solar lamps
Never walk alone after dusk near forest edges; walk in groups making gentle vocal sounds (talking, singing)
Inform the local Forest Department immediately if a wild animal is sighted near village settlements
dont: Never chase wild elephants or try to take close-up selfies with wild leopards
Never corner or throw stones at a wild animal that has entered human habitation

myths.statement: Running towards a wild leopard with sticks and flashing phone cameras will scare it away safely.
myths.truth: Surrounding and mobbing wild predators induces intense defensive panic, triggering fatal retaliatory attacks.

quiz.q: What is the single most important safety rule when walking near forest border areas after dark?
options: Travel in groups, carry a torch, and make audible vocal sounds (talking, singing)
quiz.explanation: Sound alerts wild animals from far away, allowing them to retreat into forest cover peacefully.

situations: Visiting a village near a national park buffer zone at {at}, reports indicate a wild leopard is in the vicinity.
scenario.question: What safety protocol should {name} follow?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stay indoors after dusk and keep children and domestic animals inside securely
rubric.note: Eliminates nocturnal encounter vulnerability.

rubric.point: Keep outdoor compound lights on and avoid walking alone in dark sugarcane fields
rubric.note: Illuminates surroundings and deters wildlife.
rubric.keys: keep lights on|no walking alone in dark

rubric.point: Contact the local Forest Department range office for professional tracking and safe rescue
rubric.note: Ensures scientific wildlife management.

dangerous: go hunting the leopard with sticks
take flash selfies with wild elephant

cards.title: Kite strings (Manja): The invisible killer of urban birds
facts: Glass-coated Chinese manja and nylon strings do not biodegrade, acting as razor-sharp airborne wire traps.
Thousands of pigeons, kites, owls, and fruit bats suffer amputated wings and throat slits from tangled manja.
do: Fly kites exclusively with traditional, plain cotton thread (saddi) with zero glass or metal powder coating
Fly kites in wide, open sports grounds far away from trees where birds roost and nest
Pick up and safely dispose of tangled stray kite strings found dangling in bushes or trees
dont: Never use synthetic nylon or Chinese manja (strictly banned by the National Green Tribunal)
Never fly kites near dawn and dusk when birds are actively flying to and from their nests

myths.statement: Synthetic glass-coated Chinese manja is totally legal and safe to use if you wear gloves.
myths.truth: Synthetic manja is strictly banned across India; it slashes bird wings, kills two-wheeler riders, and conducts high-voltage electricity.

quiz.q: What type of thread is safe, legal, and bird-friendly for flying kites during festivals?
options: Traditional plain cotton thread (saddi) without glass coating
quiz.explanation: Plain cotton thread snaps under tension without slicing bird flesh or human throats.

situations: During kite-flying festival celebrations at {at}, {name}'s friends want to buy sharp, banned nylon manja.
scenario.question: How can {name} champion bird-safe skies?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Insist on flying kites only with traditional plain cotton thread (saddi)
rubric.note: Eliminates razor-sharp slicing hazards for birds.
rubric.keys: plain cotton thread|saddi|no glass coating|bird safe

rubric.point: Explain that synthetic Chinese manja is illegal and kills thousands of flying birds and motorists
rubric.note: Highlights statutory ban and severe lethality.
rubric.keys: chinese manja is banned|kills birds|slashes wings

rubric.point: Avoid flying kites near trees, rooftop power lines, or bird roosting colonies
rubric.note: Reduces physical entanglement risks.

sources.name: National Green Tribunal (Ban on Synthetic Manja)

cards.title: Protecting pets and street animals during festival fireworks
facts: Dogs and cats hear acoustic frequencies up to 45,000 Hz (humans hear max 20,000 Hz) with 4x acoustic sensitivity.
High-decibel fireworks explosions cause severe acoustic trauma, heart tremors, and panic running into traffic.
do: Create a safe, cozy indoor sanctuary room: close windows, draw heavy curtains, and play soothing music/TV
Keep pet dogs on a leash during festival evening walks; ensure they wear collars with ID tags and phone numbers
Provide open stairwell or building compound shelter for terrified neighborhood street animals
dont: Never burst loud firecrackers near sleeping street animals or animal shelters
Never lock a frightened pet outdoors on a balcony where they can leap over in panic

myths.statement: Dogs who shake and cower during Diwali crackers are just acting dramatic for attention.
myths.truth: High-decibel explosions cause genuine physical agony, eardrum pain, and terrifying cardiac stress in animals.

quiz.q: Why is it essential that pet dogs wear a collar with a phone ID tag during festival cracker season?
options: Panic from explosions causes hundreds of terrified pets to bolt from gates and get lost
quiz.explanation: ID tags ensure lost, panicked pets can be quickly reunited with their families.

situations: As evening festival fireworks begin at {at}, the family dog is trembling, panting, and hiding under the bed.
scenario.question: How should {name} comfort and protect the pet?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Close all windows, draw curtains, and turn on soft background television or music to mask the noise
rubric.note: Dampens external explosion acoustic spikes.

rubric.point: Sit near the pet, speak in gentle reassuring tones, and provide a safe indoor den under blankets
rubric.note: Provides emotional security without reinforcing panic.

rubric.point: Ensure all external doors and balcony railings are securely locked so pet cannot bolt in fear
rubric.note: Prevents frantic escape and traffic accidents.

dangerous: drag trembling pet outside into fireworks

cards.title: Adopting Indie dogs: Natural resilience, loyalty and breaking breed bias
facts: Indian Pariah and Indie community dogs have evolved naturally over thousands of years to thrive in the Indian climate.
Foreign brachycephalic breeds (Pugs, Huskies, Bulldogs) suffer severe respiratory distress in hot Indian weather.
do: Adopt an Indian community dog from an animal shelter or rescue group instead of buying from commercial puppy mills
Indie dogs possess exceptional genetic immunity, rarely suffer hereditary diseases, and live long, healthy lives
Spay/neuter and vaccinate adopted Indie pets to support humane community dog population management
dont: Never buy Siberian Huskies or Saint Bernards in tropical Indian cities (it is cruelty to keep arctic dogs in 45°C heat)
Never abandon pet dogs on the streets when they grow old or fall sick

myths.statement: Foreign pedigree breed dogs are naturally smarter and more loyal than Indian stray dogs.
myths.truth: Indie dogs are among the most intelligent, resilient, loyal, and low-maintenance canine companions in the world.

quiz.q: Why are native Indian street dogs ('Indies') ideally suited for Indian family homes?
options: They are naturally adapted to the Indian climate, have strong immune systems, and are fiercely loyal

cards.title: Animals in extreme heatwaves: Water bowls, shade and heatstroke signs
facts: Urban heat island effects push city surface temperatures over 50°C, causing widespread wildlife heat collapse.
Dehydrated birds and street animals suffer kidney failure when clean drinking water is inaccessible.
do: Place wide terracotta water bowls outside your home, shops, and under shady colony trees daily
Allow street dogs and cats to rest quietly in shaded building corridors, porticos, and basements during peak heat
Notice heatstroke symptoms in animals: excessive panting, drooling, glassy eyes, and inability to stand up
dont: Never chase panting, heat-stressed animals out into scorching afternoon sun
Never pour ice-cold freezing water directly over a heatstroked animal (triggers thermal shock)

myths.statement: Street animals never feel the summer heat because they have thick fur coats to protect them.
myths.truth: Fur traps heat; street animals suffer intense dehydration, heat cramps, and heatstroke in peak summer.

quiz.q: What is the simplest community service to save urban birds and street animals during scorching June heatwaves?
options: Place wide, clean water bowls in shady spots outside homes and refill daily
quiz.explanation: Shaded water bowls provide critical hydration that prevents fatal heatstroke in urban wildlife.

cards.title: Plastic menace for cattle: Rumen impaction and wet waste rules
facts: Cows eat vegetable peelings discarded inside plastic carry bags because they smell the food inside.
Plastic bags cannot be digested; they accumulate in the cow's rumen stomach into a 50 kg concrete-like mass.
do: Never discard kitchen vegetable scraps or leftover food sealed inside plastic carry bags
Feed leftover vegetable peels to cattle in clean metal or bucket containers directly
Segregate household waste into distinct wet and dry streams so plastic never mixes with organic food
dont: Never throw plastic-wrapped food into open garbage dumps accessible to grazing cattle
Never throw sharp toothpicks, safety pins, or plastic cling film mixed with food waste

myths.statement: Cows have strong stomachs that can easily digest plastic bags and rubber wrappers safely.
myths.truth: Plastic is completely indigestible. Hundreds of kilograms of plastic accumulate inside cows' stomachs, starving them to death.

quiz.q: Why do urban cattle in India swallow dangerous plastic bags?
options: They like the taste of plastic
People throw food scraps and vegetable peels tied inside plastic bags; cows swallow the whole bag to eat the food
quiz.explanation: Cows smell the food inside thin polythene bags and swallow the entire plastic bag whole.
